newsitem.title: CHINA: ASIAN DEBT MARKETS - Ratings to the fore.
newsitem.headline: ASIAN DEBT MARKETS - Ratings to the fore.

text.p: Asian ratings were the theme on Monday in a quiet market, with agencies giving assurances on Thailand, but Indonesian state banks being put on review.
Hutchison Whampoa Finance Ltd is tipped to win an A-plus long-term credit rating for its planned US$1.0 billion 144a multi-tranche bond issue.

Standard & Poor's said it expected to assign the rating to the bond issue by Hutchison Whampoa Finance, an arm of heavyweight borrower Hutchison Whampoa, which last month signed a record HK$12 billion corporate loan.
Details of the latest U.S. dollar mutli-tranche 144a bond are sketchy, but the deal is expected to be in several tranches, and a trailblazer.
In 1994, Hongkong International Terminals Ltd, a 77.5 percent arm of Hutchison Whampoa, raised US$1.735 billion through a 10-year floating-rate note (FRN) issue mainly taken up by Hutchison Whampoa.
That deal carried a conversion option, allowing holders to swap the FRNs for transferable loan certificates.
In more rating news, bankers on Monday predicted a rating upgrade for the Philippines within one year.
"We believe that the Philippines will be upgraded in the next 12 months," said Eammon McConnell, Deutsche Morgan Grenfell managing director and head of global markets syndicate, Asia.
McConnell pointed to the falling cost of funds for Philippine Long Distance Telephone Co for example.
He said it paid 350 basis points over the 10-year U.S. Treasury in 1994 when it came to market.
In 1995, it paid 340 basis points over, in 1996, it was 240 basis points, and in 1997 it paid 150 basis points over.
Another banker predicted that short-term rates, which were squeezed upwards on Friday to help protect the peso, would fall to around 12 percent within a month.
Despite the recent flotation and develuation of the Thai baht and its economic problems, Thomson Bankwatch said it saw no reason to change its sovereign A-minus rating.

"If we believe there is an implication that we should review our rating on Thailand then we will do so," Thomson Bankwatch president Philippe Delhaise said on Monday. "But at the moment we see absolutely no reason why we should do it."
Moody's Investors Service, which downgraded Thailand's long-term sovereign rating to A3 from A2 in April, also said it had no current plans to review Thailand's rating.
But it served a warning to seven Indonesian state banks, saying their bank financial strength ratings outlook was being revised to uncertain from stable.
It said their ratings in future would depend on how they fared after a series of mergers announced last month by the Indonesian Ministry of Finance.
Hanil Bank has launched a US$100 million five-year FRN through HSBC Markets.
Issued at par, the issue was priced to yield 45 basis points over the three-month London Interbank Offered Rate, and featured puts and calls in year two.
-- Hong Kong newsroom
